summary: Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Würzburg and the University of Münster. She held posts at Notre Dame (1970–1984), Episcopal Divinity School (1984–1988), and Harvard University (1988).

Eliz Hale is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied biomedical engineering at the University of Mississippi and the University of California, Davis, and is attested as a graduate student at UC Santa Barbara in 2026.

Eliza Marian Butler studied at Newnham College, Cambridge (~1909–1913). She held posts at the University of Manchester (1936), Owens College (~1936–1945), and the University of Cambridge (~1945–1951).

Elizabeth A. Cecil works in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD at Brown under James L. Fitzgerald. Her appointments include Leiden University, the University of Groningen (2011–2013), and Florida State University (2018).

Elizabeth Colton Spooner was an Indology scholar. She studied at Harvard University under Charles Rockwell Lanman, as well as at the American Institute of Sacred Literature, Yale University, and Radcliffe College.

Elizabeth De Michelis is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from SOAS and the University of Cambridge. She served as director at Cambridge in 2000 and held a post at the University of Oxford.

Elizabeth English is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Oxford by 1999, studying under doctoral supervisor Alexis Sanderson and teacher Harunaga Isaacson.

Elizabeth Errington works in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS under Adrian David Hugh Bivar and held posts at the British Museum (1993) and the University of Oxford (~2016).

Elizabeth Guthrie is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Canterbury in 1994 and served as a tutor in religious studies at the University of Otago, attested in 2007.

Elizabeth J. Harris is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. Supervised by Ananda Guruge and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa, she studied at Kelaniya and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, later holding posts at Westminster College and Birmingham.

Elizabeth J. Perry is a sinologist and historian who studied at the University of Michigan (~1971–1978). She held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1978–1993) and Harvard University (~1997).

Elizabeth Morrison is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD from Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt, and held appointments at Amherst College (1998–1999) and Middlebury College (2003).

Elizabeth Napper is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner. She served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project, attested from 2001 to 2006.
Elizabeth Stuart is a religious studies scholar who founded Theology & Sexuality and served as Direktorin at the University of Winchester in 2021.

Elke Rogersdotter is an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. She completed her PhD at Umeå University, attested in 2006, under doctoral supervisor Thomas B. Larsson, supervisor Bozena Werbart, and co-advisors Karin Viklund and P. Ajithprasad.

Ellen M. Raven is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. She held posts at Leiden University, attested in 2003 and 2018, and on the editorial board of Gonda Indological Studies, attested in 2018.

Elliot M. Stern is an Indology scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona and Wilhelm Halbfass, and also studied under traditional teacher P. N. Pattabhirama Sastri (1978–1979).

Elliot Sperling was a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and history. He studied at Queens College, CUNY, and Indiana University Bloomington, where he later served as associate professor (1987–2015), alongside posts at Harvard and the University of Delhi.

Ellison Banks Findly is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Fred Pfeil. She held posts at Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College, Hartford, where she is attested in 1989.

Ellwood Austin Welden was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Harvard and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD ~1906). He held posts at Bryn Mawr College (1910), Lawrenceville School (-1919), and the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce (1923–1927).
